title: Weak fields, boundary power and dissipative uniqueness

items.title: Finite-energy PEC and impedance boundary formulation
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded Lipschitz polyhedron in the laboratory frame. Its boundary $\Gamma=\partial\Omega$ has the outward unit normal $n$ on the relative interior of each planar face; edge and vertex values will be irrelevant under the face-area convention below. Use the SI conventions of this framework. In particular $E$ has units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, $H$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-1}}$, $D$ has units $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, $B$ has units $\mathrm T$, and a volume current density $J$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$.

For the boundary integrals, let $\mathcal F$ be the finite family of relative interiors of the planar two-dimensional faces of $\Gamma$. Write $\lambda_2$ for Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^2$, defined as the restriction of Lebesgue outer measure to its Carath\'eodory-measurable sets; under the assumed $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, this is a complete measure. For each face $F\in\mathcal F$, let $P_F$ be its supporting plane and fix a Euclidean isometry $\iota_F:\mathbb R^2\to P_F$. For every Borel set $A\subseteq\Gamma$ (a set in the sigma-algebra generated by the open subsets of $\Gamma$), define $dS_F(A):=\lambda_2\bigl(\iota_F^{-1}(A\cap F)\bigr)$. Any two choices of $\iota_F$ differ by an affine Euclidean isometry of $\mathbb R^2$ with absolute Jacobian determinant $1$, so the Borel change-of-variables formula makes $dS_F$ independent of that choice. Each face is bounded and lies in a finite rectangle in its plane, so $dS_F(F)<\infty$. Set $dS:=\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}dS_F$ on $\Gamma$. The edges and vertices have $dS$-measure zero and are omitted, so $n$ is the outward face normal $dS$-almost everywhere; its values on edges and vertices do not affect any boundary expression. Since $dS$ is finite and Lebesgue measure restricted to $I$ is sigma-finite, $dS\otimes d\lambda_1|_I$ is the unique sigma-finite product measure on $\Gamma\times I$, with rectangle values $dS(A)\lambda_1(J)$ for Borel $A\subseteq\Gamma$ and Lebesgue-measurable $J\subseteq I$. All boundary $L^p(\Gamma)$ and $L^p(\Gamma\times I)$ spaces and almost-everywhere statements use these measures.

Every cross product in the boundary formulas is the right-handed Euclidean cross product in the positively oriented orthonormal frame basis: for $u=(u_1,u_2,u_3)$ and $v=(v_1,v_2,v_3)$, $u\times v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\,u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\,u_1v_2-u_2v_1)$, as in the cross-product definition of this library.

For a real vector field $u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, its distributional curl is the distribution defined by

$$\langle\operatorname{curl}u,\varphi\rangle=\int_\Omega u\cdot\operatorname{curl}\varphi\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3).$$

As in the real graph space definition of the imported mathematical library, $H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ consists of the $L^2$ vector fields whose distributional curl is represented by an $L^2$ vector field, with norm

$$\|u\|_{H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)}^2=\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by that imported weak-derivative convention. Let $\varepsilon,\mu:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ be measurable, essentially bounded, real symmetric coefficient fields, independent of time. Require constants $0<a_\varepsilon\le b_\varepsilon<\infty$ and $0<a_\mu\le b_\mu<\infty$ such that, for almost every $x\in\Omega$ and every $v\in\mathbb R^3$,

$$a_\varepsilon |v|^2\le v\cdot\varepsilon(x)v\le b_\varepsilon |v|^2,\qquad a_\mu |v|^2\le v\cdot\mu(x)v\le b_\mu |v|^2.$$

The coefficient units are $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, respectively. They define bounded symmetric multiplication operators on $L^2$. Define $D(t)=\varepsilon E(t)$ and $B(t)=\mu H(t)$. The spatially varying coefficient fields are explicit local model data; they are not inferred from the homogeneous material-closure postulate. Its constant symmetric branch is a special case.

A field $E:I\to L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ is in $C^1(I;L^2)$ when it has a derivative in the $L^2$ norm at every $t\in I$ and that derivative is norm-continuous. $C(I;H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega))$ means norm-continuity into the graph space. A finite-energy model solution is a pair

$$E,H\in C^1(I;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))\cap C(I;H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)),$$

with $J\in C(I;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$, satisfying the adopted evolution equations as $L^2$ identities for each $t\in I$,

$$\varepsilon\,\partial_t E=\operatorname{curl}H-J,\qquad \mu\,\partial_t H=-\operatorname{curl}E.$$

Its stored field energy is the finite real number

$$W(t):=\frac12\int_\Omega\bigl(E(x,t)\cdot\varepsilon(x)E(x,t)+H(x,t)\cdot\mu(x)H(x,t)\bigr)\,d\lambda_3(x).$$

There are two alternative boundary models.

**PEC.** Perfect electric conductor means $E(t)\in H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ for every $t$, where $H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ is exactly the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ in the displayed graph norm. This closure definition is used; it is not replaced by an unproved identification with every possible trace kernel.

**Impedance.** A Green-compatible tangential boundary pair consists of measurable fields $E_\tau,H_\tau\in L^2(\Gamma\times I;\mathbb R^3)$ with $n\cdot E_\tau=n\cdot H_\tau=0$ almost everywhere and, for almost every $t$,

$$\int_\Omega\bigl(\operatorname{curl}H\cdot E-H\cdot\operatorname{curl}E\bigr)\,d\lambda_3=-\int_\Gamma n\cdot(E_\tau\times H_\tau)\,dS.$$

This Green identity is part of impedance admissibility; membership in $H(\operatorname{curl})$ alone does not assert that such an $L^2$ pair exists. Let $Y\in L^\infty(\Gamma)$ be a time-independent scalar surface admittance, in siemens, with $Y\ge0$ almost everywhere. The impedance law is

$$H_\tau=Y(n\times E_\tau)\quad\text{almost everywhere on }\Gamma\times I.$$

Then $Y|E_\tau|^2\in L^1(\Gamma\times I)$ and is the nonnegative outward boundary-power density in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. No pointwise boundary trace of an arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ field is asserted.

references.locator: Section 5.3, printed p. 5.5 (PDF p. 65): dielectric-interface boundary conditions; Section 8.2, printed pp. 8.1-8.2 (PDF pp. 86-87): energy density, Poynting identity and fixed-volume boundary flux. These are smooth-field treatments; weak material claims below are proved locally.

references.title: Long Chen, Variational Formulation of Maxwell Equations, University of California, Irvine lecture note, updated May 12 2024, 8 pp.

items.physical_scope: A conditional, local, linear, nondispersive Maxwell boundary model in one SI inertial laboratory frame. It includes static measurable uniformly positive coefficient fields, the constant-coefficient branch of the material-closure postulate, a closure-defined PEC boundary condition, and an impedance branch only for fields carrying explicit Green-compatible L2 tangential boundary data. It asserts no existence theorem, no general L2 trace theorem, no validity for any actual material, and no empirical claim.

items.title: Weak surface divergence of a tangential field
items.statement:
Assume the surface-measure convention with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the mathematical definition of the stationary surface distribution. Let $S\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface without manifold boundary, with a chosen continuous unit normal $n$ and its finite surface measure $dS$. At $x\in S$, define the tangent plane

$$T_xS:=\{v\in\mathbb R^3:v\cdot n(x)=0\}.$$

For $\phi\in C^1(S)$, meaning that its composition with each local $C^2$ surface chart is $C^1$, its surface gradient $\nabla_S\phi(x)\in T_xS$ is the unique vector satisfying

$$v\cdot\nabla_S\phi(x)=d\phi_x(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in T_xS,$$

where $d\phi_x$ is the derivative of $\phi$ in tangent directions. For a measurable tangential field $K:S\to\mathbb R^3$ with $\int_S|K|\,dS<\infty$, define its **weak surface divergence** $\operatorname{Div}_S K$ as the linear functional on $C^1(S)$

$$\langle\operatorname{Div}_S K,\phi\rangle:=-\int_S K\cdot\nabla_S\phi\,dS.$$

This functional is well-defined because $S$ is compact, $\nabla_S\phi$ is continuous and bounded, and $K$ is integrable. If it has a continuous density $g:S\to\mathbb R$, meaning

$$\langle\operatorname{Div}_S K,\phi\rangle=\int_S g\phi\,dS\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C^1(S),$$

then $g$ is called a continuous representative of the weak surface divergence. The definition itself does not assert that such a representative exists or is unique; a result using pointwise $\operatorname{div}_S K$ must establish both.

references.title: Long Chen, Variational Formulation of Maxwell Equations, University of California, Irvine lecture note, updated May 12 2024, 8 pp.
references.locator: Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, introduces the intrinsic surface divergence/curl on tangent fields and relates them to tangential traces. The weak functional below is stated independently and explicitly.

items.title: Energy balance and forward uniqueness for admissible weak Maxwell fields
items.statement:
Use the finite-energy boundary model defined earlier on the nonempty open time interval $I$ and bounded Lipschitz polyhedron $\Omega$. Thus $\varepsilon,\mu$ are time-independent real symmetric essentially bounded coefficient fields with uniform positive lower bounds, $E,H\in C^1(I;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))\cap C(I;H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega))$, $J\in C(I;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$, and

$$\varepsilon\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}H-J,\qquad\mu\partial_tH=-\operatorname{curl}E$$

hold as $L^2$ identities for every $t\in I$. Define

$$W(t):=\frac12\int_\Omega\bigl(E\cdot\varepsilon E+H\cdot\mu H\bigr)\,d\lambda_3.$$

For every $s<t$ in $I$, the closure-defined PEC branch satisfies

$$W(t)-W(s)=-\int_s^t\int_\Omega E\cdot J\,d\lambda_3\,dr.$$

For the Green-compatible impedance branch, where $H_\tau=Y(n\times E_\tau)$, it satisfies

$$W(t)-W(s)=-\int_s^t\int_\Omega E\cdot J\,d\lambda_3\,dr-\int_s^t\int_{\partial\Omega}Y|E_\tau|^2\,dS\,dr.$$

Here $E_\tau,H_\tau$ and the Green identity are exactly the $L^2$ boundary data and admissibility condition in the model definition; no trace is inferred from H(curl) membership alone. The work density $E\cdot J$ has SI units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$; the boundary term has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ per unit area and is nonnegative in the impedance branch. If $J=0$ and $E(t_0)=H(t_0)=0$ in $L^2$, the only admissible solution is zero for $t\ge t_0$. Uniqueness is forward from the specified initial time; no backward uniqueness is asserted for a dissipative boundary.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zurich 2024 FS lecture notes, 176 pp.
references.locator: Section 8.2, printed pp. 8.1-8.2 (PDF pp. 86-87), equations (8.3)-(8.9): smooth vacuum energy density, Poynting identity and fixed-volume energy flux. The present proof derives the conditional heterogeneous H(curl) identity from its exact weak model.

references.title: Long Chen, Variational Formulation of Maxwell Equations, University of California, Irvine lecture note, updated May 12 2024, 8 pp.
references.locator: Sections 1-3.2, PDF pp. 1-5: H(curl) graph space, Green integration-by-parts formulas, PEC and impedance boundary conventions, and the distinction between weak trace spaces and ordinary L2 boundary fields.

items.physical_scope: An a-priori energy identity and forward initial-value uniqueness for the explicitly defined finite-energy Maxwell model with bounded static symmetric uniformly positive coefficients. The identity applies to the closure-defined PEC branch or to the impedance branch only when its Green-compatible L2 tangential boundary pair exists. It establishes no existence theorem, no general trace regularity, no conservation without the stated work and boundary terms, and no empirical claim.

items.title: Continuous density of the weak surface divergence for a C1 tangent field
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $S\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface without manifold boundary, with surface measure $dS$ and a chosen unit normal. Let $K$ be a $C^1$ tangential vector field on $S$, meaning that its two coordinate components in every $C^2$ surface chart are $C^1$. Then the weak surface divergence $\operatorname{Div}_S K$ defined earlier has a unique continuous density $g:S\to\mathbb R$ such that

$$\langle\operatorname{Div}_S K,\phi\rangle=\int_Sg\phi\,dS\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C^1(S).$$

In a chart $X:V\subseteq\mathbb R^2\to S$, write $K=K^1\partial_1X+K^2\partial_2X$ and let $J_X=\sqrt{\det(\partial_aX\cdot\partial_bX)_{a,b=1}^2}$ be its surface-area density. The representative satisfies

$$g(X(u))=J_X(u)^{-1}\sum_{a=1}^2\partial_a\bigl(J_X(u)K^a(u)\bigr).$$

This unique continuous representative is denoted $\operatorname{div}_S K$.

references.title: Long Chen, Variational Formulation of Maxwell Equations, University of California, Irvine lecture note, updated May 12 2024, 8 pp.
references.locator: Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, introduces intrinsic surface divergence/curl; the coordinate density formula and global continuous representative are proved here from the surface-measure interface.

items.title: Stationary sheets and charge conservation
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $U=I\times\Omega$ be a laboratory region, where $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a nonempty open interval and $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ is open. Use the field and SI conventions of [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]], and [[def-em-si-conventions]]: $E$ is measured in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, $B$ in tesla, $D$ in $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$, and $H$ in $\mathrm{A\,m^{-1}}$. Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact two-sided embedded $C^2$ hypersurface without manifold boundary, with unit normal $n$ pointing from the minus side $\Omega_-$ to the plus side $\Omega_+$; write $[F]=F_+-F_-$. Let $E,B,D,H$ be locally integrable fields with the joint one-sided spacetime $C^1$ extensions on the two sides used in the stationary-interface theorem. Let the volume charge $\rho_v$ and volume current $J_v$ be locally integrable and $C^1$ on each side with joint one-sided $C^1$ extensions to $S\times I$. Let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$, with $K\cdot n=0$. Their SI units are $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$ for $\rho_v$, $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ for $J_v$, $\mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$ for $\sigma$, and $\mathrm{A\,m^{-1}}$ for $K$.

Assume the distributional macroscopic equations with the stationary sheet source pair $\rho_f=\rho_v+\sigma\delta_S$, $J_f=J_v+K\delta_S$:

$$\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$$

on $U$. This is the thin-interface solution assumption of the adopted macroscopic model; it is not inferred from the smooth equations.

Then pointwise on $S\times I$,

$$n\cdot[D]=\sigma,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,\qquad n\times[H]=K,$$

and

$$\partial_t\sigma+\operatorname{div}_S K+n\cdot[J_v]=0.$$

Here $\operatorname{Div}_S K$ is the weak surface divergence of [[def-emx-surface-divergence]]. The proof uses [[lem-emx-surface-divergence-c1-representation]] to identify its unique continuous density for the stated $C^1$ current; $\operatorname{div}_S K$ denotes that density. The sign of $n\cdot[J_v]$ uses $[J_v]=J_{v,+}-J_{v,-}$ for the chosen normal. In the stationary-sheet vacuum model, if there is no point-source component in the interface neighbourhood and $D=\varepsilon_0E,\ H=B/\mu_0$, the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations supply the displayed macroscopic equations, so this theorem applies there as well.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zurich 2024 FS lecture notes, 176 pp.
references.locator: Section 5.3, printed p. 5.5 (PDF p. 65), equations (5.20)-(5.21): the normal-displacement and tangential-electric interface conditions derived from pillbox and loop tests. The local theorem retains its explicitly stated distributional sheet-source hypotheses.

references.title: Long Chen, Variational Formulation of Maxwell Equations, University of California, Irvine lecture note, updated May 12 2024, 8 pp.
references.locator: Section 2, PDF pp. 2-3: interface conditions for H and D with surface current and charge, followed by PEC and impedance formulations. The side ordering is checked against the library normal convention.

items.physical_scope: A conditional stationary-interface result for the distributional macroscopic Maxwell equations with locally integrable volume sources and a C1 free surface-charge/tangential-current sheet. It supplies the four jump laws and the compatible surface charge balance, and identifies the adopted vacuum stationary-sheet model as a special case. The interface is fixed and has no edge; no moving sheets, point-source collisions with the interface, existence theorem, constitutive inference or empirical claim is included.

title: Weak fields, boundary power and dissipative uniqueness — Examples

items.title: Weak Maxwell does not authorize quadratic self-energy
items.statement: Every distributional vacuum Maxwell solution with a point-charge source has a locally integrable ordinary electric-energy density $u_E=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|E|^2$ near the charge.
items.physical_scope: The ideal point-charge Coulomb field in the distributional pure electrostatic model. It is locally integrable but its ordinary quadratic electric-energy density is not locally integrable for nonzero charge, so the field lies outside the finite-energy boundary model. No claim is made about regularized or renormalized fields, particle mass, self-force, measurements, or every distributional Maxwell solution.

items.title: Positive admittance removes energy
items.statement:
Use the boundary geometry of the preceding finite-energy model, with $\Gamma=\partial\Omega$. On a flat boundary face with outward normal $n=e_z$, take a right-handed tangent basis $e_x,e_y$, with $e_z\times e_x=e_y$, and prescribe tangential boundary data $E_\tau=E_0e_x$ for $E_0\in\mathbb R$. For surface admittance $Y\ge0$, the boundary condition $H_\tau=Y(n\times E_\tau)$ gives $H_\tau=YE_0e_y$ and outward power

$$n\cdot(E_\tau\times H_\tau)=YE_0^2\ge0.$$

If the sign in the boundary law is reversed, $H_\tau=-Y(n\times E_\tau)$, the outward power is $-YE_0^2$; it is strictly inward when $YE_0^2>0$.

For the conditional energy consequence, suppose an actual finite-energy model solution exists on a nonempty open interval $I$ and bounded Lipschitz polyhedron $\Omega$: $E,H\in C^1(I;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))\cap C(I;H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega))$, $J\in C(I;L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$, the two evolution equations of the preceding boundary model hold as $L^2$ identities, and tangential boundary fields $E_\tau,H_\tau\in L^2(\Gamma\times I;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfy its Green compatibility identity. Take $Y\in L^\infty(\Gamma)$, $Y\ge0$, as in that model. If the reversed law $H_\tau=-Y(n\times E_\tau)$ holds almost everywhere on all of $\Gamma\times I$, then the model energy $W(t)=\tfrac12\int_\Omega(E\cdot\varepsilon E+H\cdot\mu H)\,d\lambda_3$ obeys

$$W(t)-W(s)=-\int_s^t\int_\Omega E\cdot J\,d\lambda_3\,dr+\int_s^t\int_\Gamma Y|E_\tau|^2\,dS\,dr\qquad(s<t).$$

In particular, if $J=0$ and the last integral is positive, the stored energy increases. This conclusion is conditional on existence of a solution satisfying the reversed law.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, ETH Zurich 2024 FS lecture notes, 176 pp.
references.locator: Section 8.2, printed pp. 8.1-8.2 (PDF pp. 86-87), equations (8.3)-(8.9): the Poynting vector is outward energy-flux density and its sign in the fixed-volume balance.

references.title: Long Chen, Variational Formulation of Maxwell Equations, University of California, Irvine lecture note, updated May 12 2024, 8 pp.
references.locator: Section 2, PDF p. 3: the impedance boundary condition is written as a relation between tangential magnetic field and tangential electric field. The sign convention is converted explicitly in the local calculation.

items.physical_scope: A local sign check for the impedance boundary condition in the finite-energy model, using an orthonormal tangent basis on a flat face. It records outward power and the corresponding sign of the energy balance; it is not an outgoing-wave model or an experiment.
